subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should OpenClaw resolve fenced `MEDIA:` tokens by keeping the no-extract parser contract and adding delivery-boundary warnings, or by changing the parser to extract fenced tokens?
rationale: The current parser intentionally preserves fenced examples to avoid mutating transcripts, while the user problem is a real silent media-delivery failure; automation should not choose that product contract while an open PR is already under maintainer review.

options.title: Warn at delivery boundary
options.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` examples as text, propagate a skipped-token signal through user-visible delivery paths, and merge the warning PR after maintainer re-review.

options.title: Extract fenced tokens
options.body: Change the parser contract so standalone fenced `MEDIA:` tokens are delivered, with tests documenting the intentional risk to code examples and transcripts.

options.title: Docs-only constraint
options.body: Treat fenced tokens as by-design invalid output and rely on prompt/docs guidance instead of adding runtime diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Warn at delivery boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` examples as text, propagate a skipped-token signal through user-visible delivery paths, and merge the warning PR after maintainer re-review.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc already left the live maintainer review that defines the pure-parser plus delivery-boundary warning direction for the candidate PR.
